cards.b: The growing connection between countries through movement of goods, money, information and people.
The stages a product passes through from raw materials to the consumer, often across several countries.
Trade, foreign investment, aid, labour, modern transport and information technology.
World Trade Organization: sets rules for international trade, settles disputes and encourages lower trade barriers.
International Monetary Fund: lends money to countries in difficulty (with conditions) and promotes financial stability.
Transnational corporation: a company operating in more than one country, e.g. Apple or Nike.

cards.f: Benefits of a TNC to the host country
cards.b: Jobs, training, tax income, infrastructure, technology and a positive multiplier effect.

cards.f: Costs of a TNC to the host country
cards.b: Profits sent abroad, low wages or poor conditions, environmental damage and loss of local firms.
Voluntary: people choose to move (e.g. work). Forced: people must leave (e.g. war, refugees).
Push: reasons to leave, e.g. unemployment, conflict. Pull: attractions, e.g. jobs, safety, better services.
Money migrants send home to their families.
Loss of educated and skilled workers from a country to another.
Large numbers of people visiting the same popular places, often on package holidays.
Responsible tourism with low environmental impact that benefits local people.

cards.f: How geopolitics affects tourism and trade
cards.b: Agreements and visa-free travel increase them; sanctions, tariffs, conflict or travel bans reduce them.

gaps.s: A company that operates in many countries is a ___ corporation.
The ___ lends money to countries and promotes financial stability.
The WTO sets rules for international ___.
Money sent home by migrants is called ___.
The loss of skilled workers from a country is ___ drain.
Refugees fleeing war are an example of ___ migration.
Tourism that protects the environment and helps local people is ___.
Profits from tourism that go to foreign companies are called ___.

short.q: Explain two factors that have contributed to a more globalised economy.
short.model: Modern transport such as container ships cuts costs of trade, and information technology lets firms manage global supply chains instantly.

short.q: Explain one positive and one negative impact of migration on a destination country.
short.model: Positive: fills labour shortages and migrants pay taxes. Negative: pressure on housing and public services.

short.q: Explain how geopolitical relationships can affect tourism.
short.model: Visa-free agreements make travel easy so tourism grows, while conflict or travel warnings between countries reduce visitor numbers.

short.q: Describe two ways tourism can be made more sustainable.
short.model: Limit visitor numbers or charge entry fees to reduce damage; use locally owned accommodation so more income stays in the community.

short.q: Suggest two reasons for the pattern of a TNC building factories in emerging countries.
short.model: Labour is cheaper and trade barriers are lower, so production costs are less and goods can be exported.
